title: Local Anesthetic and Root Canals: What to Expect
metaTitle: Local Anesthetic and Root Canals: What to Expect
metaDescription: How does freezing work for a root canal, and what if a tooth is hard to numb? Learn how local anaesthetic works and what dentists do to keep you comfortable.
excerpt: Local anaesthetic is what keeps a root canal comfortable. Here is how freezing works, why some teeth are trickier to numb, and what dentists do about it.
heroImageAlt: A dentist preparing to administer local anaesthetic to a relaxed patient.
bodyHtml:
How freezing keeps a root canal comfortable

Local anaesthetic — the "freezing" your dentist places before a root canal — works by temporarily blocking the nerves around the tooth from sending pain signals to your brain. Once the area is numb, you can expect to feel pressure, vibration, and movement during treatment, but not sharp pain. For the large majority of people this works reliably, and it is the main reason modern root canals are far more comfortable than their old reputation suggests. In the less common situation where a tooth is difficult to numb fully, dentists have several additional techniques they can use.

What the freezing feels like

To place the anaesthetic, the dentist usually dries the area and often applies a numbing gel first, then administers the local anaesthetic. You may feel a brief pinch and a sensation of pressure, which passes quickly. Over the next few minutes, your lip, tongue, cheek, or part of your jaw may start to feel fat, tingly, or heavy — that spreading numbness is a sign the anaesthetic is taking effect. Your dentist will check that the tooth is properly frozen before starting.

Why some teeth are harder to numb

Most teeth numb readily, but certain situations can make freezing less predictable:

  • "Hot" or acutely inflamed pulp. A tooth with active, intense inflammation can be more resistant to local anaesthetic because the inflamed tissue changes how the nerves respond. This is one reason a severe toothache can sometimes need extra attention to numb.
  • Lower back teeth. The anatomy of the lower jaw can make molars a little more challenging to freeze than upper teeth.
  • Individual variation. People simply differ in how they respond, and anatomy varies from person to person.

What dentists do when a tooth won't numb

If the usual approach does not fully settle the tooth, your dentist has options. These can include giving the anaesthetic more time to work, using a different injection technique that targets the nerves more directly, or placing supplementary anaesthetic closer to the tooth. The key message is that "I can still feel it" is not a reason to simply endure discomfort — it is information your dentist needs so they can adjust. Agreeing on a raised-hand signal before treatment starts makes it easy to pause.

After the freezing wears off

Numbness from local anaesthetic typically lasts a few hours. During that time, be careful not to bite your lip, cheek, or tongue, and wait until sensation returns before eating or drinking anything hot. Some tenderness around the tooth once the freezing fades is normal and usually eases over a few days.

Is the freezing safe?

Local anaesthetics used in dentistry have a long track record and are considered safe for most people when administered by a trained professional. It is important to tell your dentist about your full medical history, any medications you take, and any past reactions to anaesthetic, so they can choose the most appropriate approach for you.

Will I be numb for the rest of the day?

Usually not. Most people find the numbness fades within a few hours, though it can linger a little longer for some. Because your lip and tongue may still be numb after you leave, take care with hot drinks and chewing until normal feeling comes back.

What if I am afraid of the needle itself?

Needle anxiety is common. Topical numbing gel, a slow and steady technique, and simply letting your dental team know you are nervous can all help. If fear of injections has kept you from getting care, say so — it is a routine conversation for a dental team.

Comfort you can count on

Reliable freezing is the foundation of a comfortable root canal, and a good dentist will take the time to make sure you are properly numb before beginning and will respond if you feel anything. If you have questions about what to expect, the team at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham can walk you through the process, and you can read more about root canal therapy at the clinic before your visit.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
